recipes.name: Chicken Katsu Curry
steps: Chicken: Pound chicken thighs to even thickness. Season with salt. Dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg, coat with panko. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry: Heat oil to 340F (170C). Fry chicken until golden and cooked through, 4–6 minutes. Drain on a rack.
Curry sauce: Saute sliced onion until soft. Add cubed carrot and potato. Add water or stock to cover; simmer until vegetables are tender.
Season: Stir in Japanese curry roux blocks (or a mix of curry powder, flour, and butter). Simmer until thick. Adjust sweetness and salt.
Plate: Ladle curry over rice. Slice katsu and place on top. Serve with fukujinzuke pickles if available.

recipes.name: Miso Soup
steps: Heat stock until steaming but not boiling hard.
Place miso in a ladle; whisk with a little hot stock until smooth, then stir into the pot (do not boil hard after adding miso).
Add cubed tofu and warm through. Finish with sliced scallion and optional nori.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Salmon
steps: Glaze: Combine 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin (or sugar + water), 1 tbsp sugar, 1 grated garlic clove, and a little grated ginger. Simmer until slightly syrupy.
Fish: Pat salmon fillets dry. Season lightly with salt. Heat a pan with a little oil over medium-high.
Sear: Place salmon skin-side down (if skin-on) and cook 3–4 minutes until crisp. Flip and cook 2–3 minutes more.
Glaze: Lower heat. Pour glaze over the fish and spoon it over as it reduces, 1–2 minutes, until the salmon is coated and glossy.
Serve: With steamed rice and vegetables. Spoon extra glaze on top.

recipes.name: Tonkatsu
steps: Pound pork cutlets to even thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg, coat thoroughly with panko. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry in oil at 340–350F until golden and cooked through, 4–6 minutes. Drain.
Slice and serve with shredded cabbage and tonkatsu sauce.

recipes.name: Gyoza
steps: Filling: Mix 300g ground pork with finely chopped cabbage (squeezed dry), minced garlic, ginger, scallion, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Wrap: Place a small spoon of filling on a gyoza wrapper. Wet the edge with water. Fold and pleat to seal tightly.
Pan-fry: Heat oil in a non-stick pan. Arrange gyoza flat-side down. Fry until bottoms are golden, 2–3 minutes.
Steam: Add 1/4 cup water and cover immediately. Steam until water evaporates and wrappers are tender, 4–5 minutes.
Crisp: Uncover and let any remaining moisture evaporate so bottoms re-crisp. Serve with soy-vinegar-chili dip.

recipes.name: Ramen Shoyu Style
steps: Broth: Simmer chicken or pork bones with water, ginger, and garlic 1–2 hours (or use good store-bought stock). Strain. Season with soy sauce and a little mirin or salt to taste (shoyu style).
Toppings: Soft-boil eggs 7 minutes; ice bath and peel. Chashu pork: braise pork belly in soy, mirin, sake, and sugar until tender; slice. Slice scallions; prepare nori sheets.
Noodles: Cook fresh or dried ramen noodles according to package until springy. Drain well.
Assemble: Warm bowls. Add noodles. Ladle hot broth over. Top with chashu, halved egg, scallion, and nori.
Serve: Immediately. Offer extra soy or chili oil at the table.

recipes.name: Karaage
steps: Cut chicken into bite-size pieces. Marinate with soy, grated garlic, grated ginger, and a pinch of salt 15–30 minutes.
Coat with potato starch or a flour-starch mix. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry at 340F until deep golden and cooked through, 4–6 minutes. Drain.
Serve with lemon wedges and mayo or tare sauce.

recipes.name: Oyako Don
steps: Simmer sliced onion and chicken in a mixture of stock, soy, and sugar until chicken is cooked.
Pour beaten egg over the top; cover until egg is just set.
Slide over a bowl of hot rice. Top with scallion.

recipes.name: Yakitori
steps: Cut chicken into bite-size pieces; skewer with scallion if desired.
Grill or broil, basting with a soy-sugar tare, until cooked and glazed.
Serve hot with extra sauce.

recipes.name: Tamagoyaki
steps: Beat eggs with a little sugar and soy. Lightly oil a rectangular pan.
Pour a thin layer of egg; when almost set, roll to one side. Repeat with more egg, rolling each layer.
Turn out, shape, and slice.

recipes.name: Miso Glazed Eggplant
steps: Score eggplant and roast or pan-sear until soft.
Brush with a mixture of miso, sugar, and sesame oil.
Broil until the glaze bubbles and caramelizes.

recipes.name: Vegetable Tempura
steps: Make a thin batter with ice-cold water and flour; do not overmix.
Dip vegetables and fry in hot oil until pale and crisp.
Drain well and serve with tentsuyu or salt.

recipes.name: Okonomiyaki
steps: Mix batter with shredded cabbage and scallion.
Cook on a griddle with pork slices; flip when set.
Finish with okonomiyaki sauce, mayo, and nori.

recipes.name: Onigiri
steps: Cook sushi rice and season lightly with salt.
Shape into triangles with wet hands.
Wrap with nori strips.

recipes.name: Chirashi Sushi Bowl
steps: Season cooked rice with vinegar-style seasoning.
Arrange fish and vegetables on top.
Serve with soy and sesame.

recipes.name: Nikujaga
steps: Saute beef and onion.
Add potato, carrot, stock, soy, sugar.
Simmer until vegetables are tender.

recipes.name: Udon Noodle Soup
steps: Heat stock and season with soy.
Cook udon.
Add tofu and mushrooms. Top with scallion.

recipes.name: Agedashi Tofu
steps: Coat tofu and fry until golden.
Make tentsuyu sauce.
Pour over tofu, top with ginger and scallion.

recipes.name: Yakimeshi
steps: Stir-fry aromatics. Scramble egg.
Add cold rice and soy.
Finish with scallion.

recipes.name: Nasu Dengaku
steps: Score and roast eggplant.
Brush with sweet miso glaze.
Broil until caramelized.
